followup_explanation:
I chose Willet-235B because this is a straightforward knowledge/explanation task with no harm-adjacent or distasteful content involved, so the relevant deciding factor is raw capability.

Willet outperforms Curlew across every measured benchmark and eval dimension — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4) — and these gaps are well beyond run-to-run variance. The query also has an instruction-following component (the user explicitly wants a concise, non-rambling answer), and Willet's higher IFEval and Arena-Hard scores make it better suited to deliver an accurate, well-structured, appropriately brief response.

The task-preference notes about harm-adjacent content don't apply here, so they didn't factor into the decision. On pure capability, Willet is the clear choice.
